alicia: Heads up — Mia-edge started showing sustained GPU pod degradation at ~03:20 UTC. Autoscaler did not add nodes, eviction rate climbed. We shifted traffic to ORD backup but cost jumped because we blew past burst credit.

sam: Confirmed. Node churn looks like disk-pressure -> kubelet eviction cascade. Attached a condensed log snippet from kube-events.

sam: ```
Mar 03 03:19:58 gpu-02 kubelet: Evicting pods due to eviction threshold: nodefs.inodesFree
Mar 03 03:20:02 gpu-02 kubelet: Pod gpu-worker-7 restarted (OOM?)
Mar 03 03:20:10 cluster-autoscaler: no scale up possible: diskPressure taint prevented scheduling
```

jia: Ops-bot created incident INC-2026-482 and opened a provisional incident channel.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-482 — mia edge degraded GPU capacity. Priority: P2. Runbook: /runbooks/edge-capacity-failover

mike: We ran a manual weighted shift to ORD to protect latency. Command used (internal routing API):

mike: ```bash
curl -X POST https://routing.internal/api/shift -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"from":"mia","to":"ord","weight":0.65}'
```

tanvi: That 65% cutover was aggressive — it reduced tail latency but costed us heavy cross-region egress + burst GPU cost. Suggest default fallback weight = 0.4 and a 15m probe window.

alicia: Agreed. Proposals for the playbook update:
1) Add pre-warm check: ensure reserve pool >= 1 GPU node before any traffic shift.
2) Lower default emergency weight to 40% (0.4) and then ramp by 10% every 5m if tail-latency still > 200ms.
3) Add a disk-pressure remediation step: auto-evict non-critical cache volumes and cordon node if nodefs high.
4) Add cost-hedge flag that pauses cross-region burst if projected spend > X in last 30m.

sam: For (3) we can implement an agent check: if nodefs usage > 85% then run:

sam: ```bash
kubectl annotate node $NODE maintenance=disk-cleanup --overwrite
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
ssh admin@$NODE 'sudo rm -rf /var/tmp/cache/*; systemctl restart kubelet'
kubectl uncordon $NODE
```

jia: We should avoid force-draining GPUs during live traffic. Instead, add a cordon + schedule eviction window where we shift 20% per GPU pool before automating deletes.

mike: Action items from this thread I will own:
- A1: Implement emergency-weight default to 0.4 + ramp logic in routing-service (mike)
- A2: Add pre-warm/reserve-pool health check to failover-runbook (alicia)
- A3: Disk-pressure automated remediation prototype (sam)
- A4: Cost-hedge guardrail: routing-service consults cost-api before cross-region shifts (tanvi)
- A5: Post-incident telemetry: add metric mia.edge.evictions and mia.edge.nodefs_pct (jia)

tanvi: ETA guesses:
- A1: PR for routing-service by EOD tomorrow
- A2: Runbook doc update today, ops playbook PR by tomorrow
- A3: Prototype in staging in 3 days
- A4: Cost-hedge quick toggle in 2 days
- A5: Telemetry in 1 day

alicia: Also adding a short checklist to the runbook: "failover-cost-check" with steps: estimate 30m projected spend -> if > budget then run limited-weight failover + notify finance.

sam: Quick note: add alert rule to paging for sustained eviction rate > 5/min for 10m (pager -> eng-sre). That would have caught this earlier.

ops-bot: Updated runbook reference: /runbooks/edge-capacity-failover v2 (draft) — includes pre-warm and emergency-weight fields.

mike: I'll open the routing-service PR now and tag everyone for review. Planning a dry-run of the new weight-ramp in staging tomorrow 14:00 UTC.

alicia: Thanks — once PRs land let's schedule a short ops walkthrough. Leaving this thread open for updates and to collect post-incident notes and cost reconciliation.

jia: FYI — adding a postmortem stub to the incident tracker with the action items listed above.

mike: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/478 (WIP)

tanvi: Noted. I'll also add an alert to billing when cross-region egress > $2k in 30m so cost-hedge triggers earlier.

alicia: Good call. Closing summary: cause = node disk-pressure -> eviction cascade -> autoscaler blocked by taint -> fallback executed manually -> cost spike. Mitigations: playbook + routing defaults + disk-agent + cost-guard.

sam: Adding one last ops nudge: can we add a lightweight kubelet health probe that reports nodefs in metrics feed? That would simplify alerting.

alicia: Marking thread for follow-up; will update runbook and incident ticket after merges. :thumbsup:
